title: A/R Summary sorts names that start with a punctuation mark by character
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role, with {Location-A} as your current location.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Four customers have open invoices on today's date: {Customer-A}, {Customer-B}, {Customer-C} and {Customer-D}. After the same first words, {Customer-A}'s name goes on with "#", {Customer-B}'s with "-", {Customer-C}'s with a digit and {Customer-D}'s with "@".
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S1-16 #1 Diesel, {Customer-B} is ZZAUTOTEST S1-16 -1 Diesel, {Customer-C} is ZZAUTOTEST S1-16 10 Trucking and {Customer-D} is ZZAUTOTEST S1-16 @Home Towing.
  • Starting screen: A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu) is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps: 1. Without clicking any column header, find the four customers in the list.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: all four customers are listed, reading from top to bottom {Customer-A}, {Customer-B}, {Customer-C}, {Customer-D}: plain character order, where "#" comes before "-", both come before the digits, and "@" comes after them.

Held for the PO: the PRD says names compare "in plain character order: digits and punctuation compare as characters", the way QuickBooks orders them, which this case follows. The tech plan (21 Oct 2026) says the developers' order puts every punctuation mark before every digit and orders the marks differently ("-" before "#"), which would give {Customer-B} first, then {Customer-A} and {Customer-D}, then {Customer-C}. Question 16 asks Chris Ward which order is right.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 5 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11531 (Story 1, Reports open in QuickBooks name order)

  • S1-R2: “Name order compares names ignoring capitals, in plain character order: digits and punctuation compare as characters, so "10 Trucking" comes before "2 Trucking" and "A-1 Towing" before "a1 towing".”
  • Key Decisions, name order: “Names sort the way QuickBooks sorts them: plain character order, capitals ignored, accented letters with their base letter.”

From: Tech plan "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter — Technical Implementation Plan" (2026-10-21, uploaded 22 Oct 2026), read 22 Oct 2026

  • Tech plan §9 Performance: “Name order is UCA order (utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci): every PRD example holds, but punctuation sorts below digits and punctuation marks order among themselves differently from ASCII (e.g. - before #).”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
